title: Flying with a Dog on Aegean Airlines
description: Complete guide to travelling with your dog on Aegean Airlines, including cabin travel, hold transport, restrictions, booking advice and international regulations.
html:
Overview

Aegean Airlines is Greece's largest airline and a member of Star Alliance. Operating primarily from Athens International Airport (ATH) and Thessaloniki Airport (SKG), Aegean serves more than 160 destinations across Greece, Europe, the Middle East and selected destinations in North Africa.

For travellers flying with a dog, Aegean is widely recognised as one of Europe's most pet-friendly airlines. Depending on your dog's size and destination, pets may travel in the passenger cabin or in the aircraft's climate-controlled hold. Animals exceeding the airline's operational limits may require specialised cargo transport according to local regulations.

A successful journey always depends on three independent factors:

  • Aegean Airlines' pet transport policy;
  • veterinary and customs regulations of the destination country;
  • operational constraints such as aircraft type, weather, routing and available pet capacity.

MyDogCanFly analyses all three before recommending an itinerary.

👎 Main limitationsSnub-nosed breeds excluded from the hold

Why MyDogCanFly gives Aegean Airlines 4.5/5

Strengths

  • Small dogs travel in the cabin (up to 8 kg)
  • Medium and large dogs accepted in the hold
  • Extensive international network

Limitations

  • Snub-nosed breeds excluded from the hold
  • Reservation required and limited pet capacity
  • Destination-country import paperwork required

Is Aegean Airlines a good choice?

Yes. Aegean is consistently ranked among Europe's best regional airlines and has developed a clear and well-structured pet policy. Its main strengths include pets accepted in both cabin and hold, an extensive domestic Greek network, a strong European route network, a modern Airbus fleet, and competitive pet transport fees. It is particularly well suited for travellers flying to the Greek islands or Southern Europe.

Cabin, hold or cargo

Cabin transport: accepted in the cabin

Small dogs may travel inside the passenger cabin in an airline-approved carrier placed beneath the seat. Cabin transport depends on the maximum combined weight, carrier dimensions, and available pet capacity. Pets must remain inside their carrier throughout the flight.

Hold transport: accepted in the hold

Dogs exceeding cabin limits may travel inside the aircraft's ventilated and temperature-controlled hold. The kennel must comply with IATA Live Animals Regulations and provide sufficient room for the dog to stand, turn around and lie comfortably. Some aircraft types may have additional size limitations.

Breed restrictions: restrictions may apply by breed, season and destination

Certain brachycephalic breeds and some powerful breeds may be subject to operational restrictions. Always verify eligibility before purchasing your ticket.

Travel Difficulty

🟡 Moderate

Generally straightforward, but reservation is required, pet capacity is limited and destination-country paperwork must be checked.

Before booking

Before confirming your reservation:

  • verify destination-country import rules;
  • ensure your dog is microchipped and vaccinated;
  • select an IATA-compliant carrier or kennel;
  • reserve your dog's place with Aegean.

Pet acceptance depends on aircraft type and available capacity. During the summer season, pet allocations often fill quickly.

Connecting through Athens

Athens International Airport is Aegean's primary hub. For the smoothest experience, remain on Aegean-operated flights whenever possible, verify pet acceptance on partner airlines, and avoid short connections if your dog travels in the hold. Keeping the itinerary entirely on Aegean generally simplifies transfers.

Common mistakes

Waiting too long before reserving pet space

Only a limited number of pets are accepted on each aircraft.

Using a non-compliant kennel

Hold transport requires an IATA-compliant kennel.

Forgetting destination-country regulations

Airline approval never replaces veterinary or customs requirements.

Booking partner flights without checking

Codeshare airlines may apply completely different pet policies.

Expert advice

Aegean is one of the easiest airlines for travelling with a dog within Southern Europe. Its extensive domestic Greek network, modern fleet and straightforward procedures make it particularly attractive for travellers heading to the Greek islands or connecting through Athens. For the easiest journey, reserve your pet immediately after booking your ticket and keep your itinerary entirely on Aegean-operated flights whenever possible.

FAQ

Can my dog travel in the cabin?

accepted in the cabin

Can large dogs travel?

accepted in the hold

Should I reserve early?

Yes. Only a limited number of pets are accepted on each flight.

Do destination-country regulations still apply?

Always. Aegean Airlines' approval never replaces veterinary, customs or quarantine requirements imposed by the destination country.

Aegean Airlines est la principale compagnie aérienne grecque et un membre de Star Alliance. Depuis ses hubs de l'aéroport international d'Athènes (ATH) et de Thessalonique (SKG), elle dessert plus de 160 destinations en Grèce, en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord.

Pour les propriétaires de chiens, Aegean est considérée comme l'une des compagnies européennes les plus accueillantes. Selon la taille de ton animal et ta destination, ton chien peut voyager en cabine ou en soute climatisée. Comme toujours, un voyage réussi repose sur trois éléments :

  • Petits chiens acceptés en cabine (jusqu'à 8 kg)
  • Chiens moyens et grands acceptés en soute

Limites

  • Réservation obligatoire et capacité limitée
  • Formalités d'importation du pays de destination à prévoir

Aegean Airlines est-elle un bon choix ?

Oui. Aegean figure régulièrement parmi les meilleures compagnies régionales d'Europe et propose une politique claire et bien adaptée aux voyageurs accompagnés d'un chien. Ses principaux avantages sont les animaux acceptés en cabine et en soute, un réseau domestique très développé en Grèce, de nombreuses destinations européennes, une flotte moderne composée principalement d'Airbus, et des tarifs généralement compétitifs pour le transport des animaux. Pour voyager vers les îles grecques ou l'Europe du Sud, Aegean constitue souvent l'une des meilleures options.

Cabine, soute ou fret

Transport en cabine : accepté en cabine

Les petits chiens peuvent voyager en cabine dans un sac homologué placé sous le siège devant toi. L'acceptation dépend du poids total autorisé, des dimensions du sac, et du nombre maximal d'animaux déjà enregistrés sur le vol. Ton chien doit rester dans son sac pendant toute la durée du voyage.

Transport en soute : accepté en soute

Les chiens dépassant les limites de la cabine voyagent dans une soute ventilée, pressurisée et climatisée. La caisse doit respecter les normes IATA Live Animals Regulations et permettre au chien de se tenir debout naturellement, de se retourner, et de s'allonger confortablement. Selon le type d'appareil, certaines limitations de dimensions peuvent s'appliquer.

Restrictions de races : des restrictions peuvent s'appliquer selon la race, la saison et la destination

Certaines races brachycéphales (nez écrasé) ainsi que quelques races puissantes peuvent être soumises à des restrictions supplémentaires. Il est recommandé de vérifier l'éligibilité de ton chien avant toute réservation.

Difficulté du voyage

🟡 Modéré

Voyage généralement simple, mais réservation obligatoire, capacité limitée et formalités du pays de destination à vérifier.

Avant de réserver

Avant d'acheter ton billet :

  • vérifie les formalités du pays de destination ;
  • assure-toi que ton chien est identifié et correctement vacciné ;
  • choisis un sac ou une caisse conforme aux normes IATA ;
  • demande la réservation de ton chien auprès d'Aegean Airlines.

Le nombre d'animaux accepté dépend du type d'appareil et reste limité sur chaque vol. En haute saison, les capacités sont souvent atteintes plusieurs semaines avant le départ.

Les correspondances à Athènes

L'aéroport international d'Athènes constitue le principal hub d'Aegean. Pour voyager sereinement, privilégie un itinéraire entièrement opéré par Aegean, vérifie les conditions appliquées par les compagnies partenaires, et évite les correspondances trop courtes si ton chien voyage en soute. Un itinéraire 100 % Aegean simplifie généralement les transferts.

Erreurs fréquentes

Attendre avant de réserver la place du chien

Le nombre d'animaux accepté sur chaque appareil est limité.

Utiliser une caisse non conforme

Le transport en soute nécessite obligatoirement une caisse conforme aux normes IATA.

Oublier les formalités du pays

L'autorisation délivrée par la compagnie ne remplace jamais les obligations vétérinaires ou douanières.

Réserver un vol opéré par un partenaire sans vérifier sa politique

Les compagnies partenaires peuvent appliquer des règles totalement différentes concernant les animaux.

Conseil d'expert

Aegean Airlines est probablement l'une des meilleures compagnies pour voyager avec un chien en Méditerranée. Son réseau très dense vers les îles grecques, sa flotte moderne et ses procédures simples en font un excellent choix aussi bien pour les vacances que pour les voyages réguliers. Pour une expérience optimale, réserve ton chien dès l'achat du billet et privilégie un itinéraire entièrement opéré par Aegean.

FAQ

Mon chien peut-il voyager en cabine ?

accepté en cabine

Les grands chiens sont-ils acceptés ?

accepté en soute

Dois-je réserver longtemps à l'avance ?

Oui. Le nombre d'animaux accepté étant limité sur chaque vol, une réservation anticipée est fortement recommandée.

Les formalités du pays restent-elles obligatoires ?

Toujours. L'autorisation délivrée par Aegean Airlines ne remplace jamais les exigences vétérinaires, douanières ou de quarantaine imposées par le pays de destination.

Is Air Canada a good choice?

Yes. Air Canada is one of the most pet-friendly major airlines in North America. Its strengths include pets accepted both in the cabin and in the baggage compartment, an extensive domestic and international network, a dedicated AC Animals cargo service, a modern long-haul fleet, and clear online guidance for pet travel. For owners of both small and large dogs, Air Canada offers considerably more flexibility than many U.S. carriers.

Cabin, hold or cargo

Cabin transport: One cat or small dog per passenger; soft-sided carrier under the seat; pet at least 10 weeks old.

Small dogs may travel in the passenger cabin inside a soft-sided carrier that fits completely beneath the seat in front of you. Beginning 1 June 2025, Air Canada requires all in-cabin pets to travel in soft-sided carriers. Cabin pets are not permitted in certain seating locations (such as exit rows or bulkhead seats), and space is limited on every flight.

Hold transport: Hard-sided kennel; pet plus kennel max 45 kg; snub-nosed breeds barred; seasonal heat/cold embargoes; no pets 18 Dec–4 Jan.

Dogs exceeding cabin limits may travel in the aircraft's ventilated and temperature-controlled baggage compartment inside an IATA-compliant kennel. On most routes, the combined weight of the dog and kennel must not exceed 45 kg (100 lb). Larger kennels or heavier animals generally require transport through Air Canada Cargo (AC Animals). Seasonal heat restrictions also apply on certain routes and destinations.

Breed restrictions: snub-nosed breeds face additional restrictions; heat embargoes may apply in the hold

Certain brachycephalic breeds and specific operational situations may result in additional restrictions. Heat embargoes may also temporarily prevent transport in the baggage compartment.

Travel Difficulty

🟡 Moderate

Generally straightforward, but reservation is required, pet capacity is limited and destination-country paperwork must be checked.

Before booking

Before confirming your reservation:

  • verify destination-country import requirements;
  • ensure your dog is properly identified and vaccinated;
  • choose an IATA-compliant carrier or kennel;
  • register your pet with Air Canada.

Air Canada strongly recommends registering pets within 24 hours of booking to guarantee availability. Pets that have not been registered in advance may not be accepted for travel.

Connecting through Canada

Toronto, Montréal and Vancouver are major international hubs. Whenever possible, remain on Air Canada-operated flights, verify every codeshare segment, and avoid long connections if your dog travels in the baggage compartment. Remember that many partner airlines apply different pet policies.

Common mistakes

Waiting too long before registering your dog

Pet capacity is limited on every aircraft.

Using a hard-sided carrier in the cabin

Since June 2025, Air Canada requires soft-sided carriers for all pets travelling in the cabin.

Forgetting seasonal embargoes

Some destinations prohibit baggage-compartment pet transport during hot weather.

Booking codeshare flights without checking

Not every flight marketed by Air Canada is operated by Air Canada, and partner airlines may refuse pets.

Expert advice

Air Canada is one of the strongest choices in North America for travelling with a dog. Unlike several U.S. airlines, it still offers both cabin and checked hold transport on many routes, while also providing a dedicated cargo solution for oversized animals. For the smoothest experience, register your dog immediately after booking your ticket and keep your itinerary entirely on Air Canada-operated flights whenever possible.

Can my dog travel in the cabin?

One cat or small dog per passenger; soft-sided carrier under the seat; pet at least 10 weeks old.

Can large dogs travel?

Hard-sided kennel; pet plus kennel max 45 kg; snub-nosed breeds barred; seasonal heat/cold embargoes; no pets 18 Dec–4 Jan.

Should I register my dog immediately?

Yes. Air Canada recommends registering your pet within 24 hours of booking, as cabin and hold capacity is limited.

Do destination-country regulations still apply?

Always. Air Canada's approval never replaces veterinary, customs or quarantine requirements imposed by the destination country.

Overview

British Airways is the United Kingdom's flag carrier and a founding member of the oneworld Alliance. Operating primarily from London Heathrow (LHR) and London Gatwick (LGW), it serves more than 200 destinations across Europe, North America, Africa, Asia, the Middle East and Oceania.

For travellers flying with a dog, British Airways is very different from most European airlines. With the exception of recognised assistance dogs, companion animals are not accepted in the passenger cabin or as checked baggage. Instead, they normally travel through IAG Cargo, the specialist animal transport division serving British Airways and several other airlines. This policy is largely influenced by the United Kingdom's animal import regulations.

A successful journey depends on three independent elements:

  • British Airways' transport policy;
  • destination-country veterinary and customs requirements;
  • operational constraints such as aircraft type, routing, weather and cargo availability.

Is British Airways a good choice?

Yes—but only if you understand its specific model. Unlike most European airlines, British Airways has chosen to centralise companion animal transport through IAG Cargo, providing specialised handling from departure to arrival. Its main strengths include professional live-animal handling, a worldwide long-haul network, strong expertise for international relocations, and dedicated cargo facilities at Heathrow. For owners of small dogs hoping to travel in the cabin, however, British Airways is generally not the right choice.

Cabin, cargo or assistance dogs

Cabin transport: Pets are not accepted in the cabin on any route; only assistance dogs travel in the cabin, free of charge.

Companion dogs are not accepted in the passenger cabin. The only exception concerns recognised assistance dogs travelling with eligible passengers on approved routes and subject to documentation requirements.

Cargo transport: Pets travel in the hold but not as passenger checked baggage — arrangements are made via IAG Cargo (to the UK) or PetAir UK (exports).

Most dogs travel through IAG Cargo's Pet Transport service. Animals are transported in IATA-compliant kennels and handled by dedicated live-animal teams throughout the journey. Depending on the route, bookings are made either directly with IAG Cargo or through an approved pet relocation company.

Breed restrictions: restrictions may apply by breed, season and destination

Certain brachycephalic breeds and breeds subject to national legislation may face additional transport restrictions. Destination-country regulations may also prohibit entry for specific breeds.

Travel Difficulty

Several operational constraints: dogs travel in the hold or as specialised cargo, with more documentation and preparation.

Before purchasing your ticket:

  • ensure your dog's microchip and vaccinations are compliant;
  • contact IAG Cargo or an approved pet shipper;
  • prepare an IATA-compliant kennel.

Unlike traditional airlines, booking your own passenger ticket does not automatically reserve transport for your dog.

Connecting through London

London Heathrow is one of the world's busiest international cargo hubs. Whenever possible, avoid unnecessary transfers, verify that every flight is operated by British Airways or another airline accepting live animals, and allow sufficient connection time for cargo processing.

Common mistakes

Assuming pets can travel in the cabin

They cannot, except recognised assistance dogs.

Booking your own ticket without arranging cargo

Passenger and pet reservations are handled separately.

Forgetting UK import regulations

The United Kingdom has specific animal health requirements that differ from many EU countries.

Using a non-IATA kennel

IAG Cargo requires compliant transport containers.

Expert advice

British Airways is an excellent airline for international pet relocation, but it is not designed for typical holiday travel with a small dog. If your goal is to keep your dog with you in the cabin, airlines such as Air France, Lufthansa or KLM will generally be more suitable. If you are relocating internationally with a large dog, however, British Airways and IAG Cargo are among the world's leading specialist operators.

Can my dog travel in the cabin?

Pets are not accepted in the cabin on any route; only assistance dogs travel in the cabin, free of charge.

Can large dogs travel?

Pets travel in the hold but not as passenger checked baggage — arrangements are made via IAG Cargo (to the UK) or PetAir UK (exports).

Are assistance dogs accepted?

Yes. Recognised assistance dogs may travel in the cabin on eligible routes, subject to British Airways' documentation requirements.

Do UK import regulations still apply?

Always. British Airways and IAG Cargo approval never replaces veterinary, customs or quarantine requirements imposed by the United Kingdom or your destination country.

Corsair is a French airline specializing in long-haul services between mainland France, the French overseas territories, Africa and the Indian Ocean. From its main base at Paris-Orly Airport (ORY), it serves destinations including Guadeloupe, Martinique, Réunion, Mayotte, Madagascar, Côte d'Ivoire and Mauritius.

For travellers flying with a dog, Corsair offers one of the most flexible pet policies among French long-haul airlines. Depending on your dog's size, pets may travel in the passenger cabin or in the aircraft's climate-controlled hold. Animals exceeding the maximum permitted weight must travel as cargo.

A successful journey depends on three independent factors:

Is Corsair a good choice?

Yes. Corsair is particularly attractive for travellers flying to French overseas destinations with their dog. Its main strengths include pets accepted in both cabin and hold, long-haul expertise, excellent coverage of French overseas territories, and dedicated procedures for pet transport. For French travellers heading to Martinique, Guadeloupe or Réunion, Corsair is one of the leading options.

Cabin, hold or cargo

Cabin transport: accepted in the cabin

Small dogs may travel inside the passenger cabin in an approved carrier placed beneath the seat. Current policy includes one pet per passenger; advance reservation required; pets must remain inside the carrier throughout the flight; and pets are not accepted in the cabin on routes to or from Mauritius.

Hold transport: accepted in the hold

Dogs exceeding the cabin weight limit must travel in the aircraft's ventilated and temperature-controlled hold. The kennel must comply with IATA Live Animals Regulations. Current policy also states a maximum combined weight (dog + kennel) of 50 kg; above 50 kg, transport must be arranged as cargo; and veterinary health documentation is required before departure.

Breed restrictions: restrictions may apply by breed, season and destination

Certain brachycephalic breeds are not accepted in the hold because of increased respiratory risks. French Category 1 dogs are prohibited, while some Category 2 dogs may travel subject to strict legal requirements and documentation.

Travel Difficulty

🟡 Moderate

Generally straightforward, but reservation is required, pet capacity is limited and destination-country paperwork must be checked.

Before booking

Before purchasing your ticket:

  • verify destination-country veterinary requirements;
  • ensure your dog is microchipped and vaccinated;
  • reserve pet transport at least 72 hours before departure;
  • prepare an IATA-compliant kennel if travelling in the hold.

Waiting too long before reserving your dog

Corsair requires advance reservation and pet capacity is limited.

Forgetting destination-specific restrictions

Some destinations—such as Mauritius—apply additional rules regarding pets travelling in the cabin.

Using a non-compliant kennel

Hold transport requires an IATA-approved rigid kennel.

Ignoring veterinary paperwork

Health certificates and vaccination requirements vary depending on the destination country.

Expert advice

Corsair is one of the best airlines for travelling with a dog between mainland France and the French overseas territories. Because several destinations apply additional veterinary rules, we recommend preparing your paperwork well in advance and reserving your dog's place as soon as you book your ticket.

Can my dog travel in the cabin?

accepted in the cabin

Can large dogs travel?

accepted in the hold

Yes. Corsair requires pet reservations to be made before departure, and capacity is limited.

Do destination-country regulations still apply?

Always. Corsair's approval never replaces veterinary, customs or quarantine requirements imposed by the destination country.

Owners of large dogs should carefully review Delta Cargo requirements before booking.

Cabin, hold or cargo

Cabin transport: Soft-sided kennel fully under the seat; at least 8 weeks old; booked by phone.

Small dogs may travel inside the passenger cabin in an airline-approved carrier that fits completely beneath the seat. Only a limited number of pets are accepted in each cabin, so reservations should be made as early as possible. Pets must remain inside their carrier throughout boarding and the flight.

Cargo transport: Checked pets accepted only for active-duty U.S. military and State Department Foreign Service personnel.

Unlike many European airlines, Delta generally does not offer accompanied checked-pet transport for large companion animals. Most larger pets travel through Delta Cargo, and this service is currently restricted primarily to active U.S. military personnel and U.S. Foreign Service Officers relocating under official orders. Some international destinations also require cargo transport regardless of the airline's own policy.

For most passengers, Delta now requires cargo transport for larger animals.

CDC requirements may apply even when returning to the United States.

Partner airlines may have completely different pet policies.

Expert advice

Delta is an excellent airline for travelling with a small dog in the cabin, particularly within North America. For owners of large dogs, planning requires much more preparation because Delta's traditional checked-pet service has been significantly reduced in favour of specialised cargo transport. If your itinerary includes international travel, always verify both Delta's policy and your destination country's import regulations before booking.

Hold transport: not accepted in the hold

Eurowings does not transport companion dogs in the aircraft hold. Travellers with medium or large dogs should select another airline that offers checked pet transport.

As with any trip to Japan, the airline is only one part of the process—the import regulations are equally important.

Cabin, hold or assistance dogs

Cabin transport: not accepted in the cabin

Companion dogs are not accepted in the passenger cabin. Only recognised assistance dogs travelling with eligible passengers may remain in the cabin.

Hold transport: accepted in the hold

Companion dogs travel inside the aircraft's ventilated and temperature-controlled hold. Requirements include advance reservation; an IATA-compliant rigid kennel; valid veterinary documentation; and acceptance depending on aircraft type and weather conditions. Certain extreme temperatures may temporarily suspend pet transport.

Breed restrictions: restrictions may apply by breed, season and destination

Certain brachycephalic breeds may be restricted because of increased respiratory risks. Additional seasonal restrictions may also apply.

Travel Difficulty

🔴 Expert

Long administrative preparation: import permits, official approval and possible quarantine depending on origin (Australia, Japan, French Polynesia…).

Before booking

Before purchasing your ticket:

  • verify Japan's import regulations;
  • ensure your dog has an ISO-compatible microchip;
  • complete all rabies vaccination requirements;
  • perform the rabies antibody blood test if required;
  • notify Japan's Animal Quarantine Service within the required deadline;
  • reserve your dog's transport with Japan Airlines.

Failure to comply with Japan's import rules may result in quarantine or refusal of entry even if your flight reservation has been confirmed.

Preparation may require several months.

Assuming airline approval guarantees entry

Only the Japanese authorities decide whether an animal may enter the country.

Using a kennel that does not meet IATA standards

Only compliant kennels are accepted.

Ignoring seasonal restrictions

Weather conditions may affect the transport of certain breeds.

Japan Airlines is one of the best airlines for travelling with a dog to Japan. The most important part of the journey is preparing Japan's import documentation. Begin planning several months before departure and ensure every veterinary requirement has been completed before booking your flight.

Overview

KLM Royal Dutch Airlines is the national airline of the Netherlands and a founding member of the Air France–KLM Group and the SkyTeam alliance. Operating primarily from Amsterdam Airport Schiphol (AMS), KLM serves more than 160 destinations across Europe, North America, South America, Africa, Asia and the Caribbean.

For travellers flying with a dog, KLM is one of Europe's most pet-friendly network airlines. Depending on your dog's size, breed and destination, pets may travel in the passenger cabin or in the aircraft's climate-controlled hold. Certain destinations or oversized animals may require cargo transport.

A successful journey always depends on three independent factors:

  • KLM's transport policy;
  • veterinary and customs regulations of the destination country;
  • operational constraints such as aircraft type, weather, routing and available pet capacity.

  • Small dogs travel in the cabin (up to 8 kg)
  • Medium and large dogs accepted in the hold
  • Extensive international network

Limitations

  • Snub-nosed breeds excluded from the hold
  • Reservation required and limited pet capacity
  • Destination-country import paperwork required

Is KLM a good choice?

Absolutely. KLM has long been recognised as one of Europe's leading airlines for travelling with pets. Its main strengths include pets accepted in both cabin and hold, an excellent worldwide network, a highly efficient hub at Amsterdam Schiphol, harmonised procedures with Air France, and reliable long-haul operations. For many international journeys, KLM offers one of the smoothest experiences available.

Cabin, hold or cargo

Cabin transport: One pet in Economy (or Business within Europe); stays in the kennel throughout; minimum 15 weeks old.

One cat or one dog may travel in the passenger cabin when flying in Economy Class or Business Class within Europe. The combined weight of the pet and carrier must not exceed 8 kg, and the carrier must fit beneath the seat in front of you. Pets must remain inside the carrier throughout the flight. Cabin transport is not available in Premium Comfort or intercontinental Business Class, where under-seat space is insufficient.

Hold transport: Up to 3 pets; pet plus kennel max 75 kg; snub-nosed breeds not accepted; no pets to the UK.

Dogs exceeding the cabin limit may travel in the aircraft's ventilated and temperature-controlled hold inside an IATA-compliant kennel. The combined weight of the dog and kennel may not exceed 75 kg. Certain aircraft have additional kennel size limitations, and pets are generally not accepted in the hold when a connection exceeds three hours. Some destinations also require transport via cargo.

Breed restrictions: snub-nosed breeds face additional restrictions

Certain brachycephalic breeds and other breeds presenting increased transport risks may be subject to operational restrictions. Always verify eligibility before booking.

Travel Difficulty

🟡 Moderate

Generally straightforward, but reservation is required, pet capacity is limited and destination-country paperwork must be checked.

Before booking

Before confirming your reservation:

  • verify destination-country import requirements;
  • ensure your dog is microchipped and properly vaccinated;
  • select an IATA-compliant carrier or kennel;
  • reserve your dog's place with KLM.

KLM requests that pet reservations be completed at least 48 hours before departure, although booking immediately after purchasing your ticket is strongly recommended because pet capacity is limited.

Connecting through Amsterdam

Amsterdam Schiphol is one of Europe's largest transfer hubs. For the easiest experience, keep your itinerary entirely on KLM whenever possible, verify pet acceptance on all codeshare flights, and avoid long layovers if your dog travels in the hold. Because Air France and KLM share similar procedures, connections within the Air France–KLM Group are usually straightforward.

Common mistakes

Waiting too long before reserving your pet

Pet capacity is limited on every flight.

Choosing a kennel that is too large or too small

Both weight and external dimensions must comply with KLM's limits.

Forgetting country-specific regulations

Import permits, veterinary certificates and quarantine rules remain the passenger's responsibility.

Assuming partner airlines apply KLM rules

Codeshare flights may follow completely different pet policies.

Expert advice

KLM is one of the best airlines in Europe for travelling with a dog. Its combination of flexible cabin transport, reliable hold facilities and the exceptional connectivity of Amsterdam Schiphol makes it suitable for almost every type of international journey. For the smoothest experience, reserve your dog's place immediately after booking your ticket and, whenever possible, remain on flights operated exclusively by KLM or Air France.

FAQ

Can my dog travel in the cabin?

One pet in Economy (or Business within Europe); stays in the kennel throughout; minimum 15 weeks old.

Can large dogs travel?

Up to 3 pets; pet plus kennel max 75 kg; snub-nosed breeds not accepted; no pets to the UK.

Should I reserve early?

Yes. KLM recommends booking your pet at least 48 hours before departure, but earlier is always better because the number of animals accepted on each flight is limited.

Do destination-country regulations still apply?

Always. KLM approval never replaces veterinary, customs or quarantine requirements imposed by the destination country.

Les petits chiens et chats peuvent voyager en cabine dans un sac souple homologué placé sous le siège devant toi.

Les conditions de transport en soute sont : Les chiens voyagent en bagage enregistré en soute ; animal + caisse jusqu'à 45 kg (100 lb) ; caisse maximale 101 × 68 × 81 cm.

Les chiens plus grands peuvent voyager dans une caisse homologuée IATA installée dans une soute ventilée et pressurisée. Selon certains itinéraires, le transport peut être assuré via WestJet Cargo.

Les éventuelles restrictions concernant certaines races sont : des restrictions peuvent s'appliquer selon la race, la saison et la destination

Comme toujours, ces règles concernent uniquement le transport aérien. Les exigences vétérinaires restent celles du pays de destination.

Difficulté du voyage

🟡 Modéré

Voyage généralement simple, mais réservation obligatoire, capacité limitée et formalités du pays de destination à vérifier.

Avant de réserver

Avant d'acheter ton billet :

  • vérifie la disponibilité pour ton chien ;
  • contrôle son poids de voyage ;
  • mesure précisément le sac ou la caisse ;
  • consulte les formalités du pays d'arrivée.

WestJet recommande de réserver le transport de l'animal dès la confirmation du billet. Les capacités sont limitées sur chaque vol.

Les correspondances

Lorsque cela est possible, privilégie un vol direct. Si ton voyage comprend une autre compagnie aérienne, vérifie que celle-ci accepte également les animaux selon des conditions compatibles. Certaines liaisons en partage de code (codeshare) ne permettent pas le transport des animaux.

Erreurs fréquentes

Réserver le billet avant la place du chien

Le nombre d'animaux autorisés est limité sur chaque vol.

Choisir un sac ou une caisse non conforme

Les dimensions sont systématiquement contrôlées lors de l'enregistrement.

Oublier les restrictions liées aux températures

Comme plusieurs compagnies nord-américaines, WestJet peut limiter le transport en soute lors d'épisodes de fortes chaleurs ou de grand froid.

Penser que tous les vols opérés sous le numéro WestJet acceptent les animaux

Les vols assurés par des compagnies partenaires peuvent appliquer des règles différentes.

Conseil d'expert

WestJet est probablement l'une des meilleures compagnies pour voyager avec un chien à l'intérieur du Canada. Lorsque cela est possible, choisis un vol direct opéré par WestJet. Tu limiterez les manipulations de ton chien, réduirez le stress lié aux correspondances et bénéficierez d'une organisation plus simple.

FAQ

Mon chien peut-il voyager en cabine ?

Petits animaux uniquement : le chien doit tenir dans un sac souple placé entièrement sous le siège (max 41 × 21,5 × 25,4 cm) et pouvoir se tenir debout, se retourner et se coucher. Un animal par passager. Pas de limite de poids publiée, mais la taille du sac limite de fait la cabine aux petits chiens.

Les grands chiens sont-ils acceptés ?

Les chiens voyagent en bagage enregistré en soute ; animal + caisse jusqu'à 45 kg (100 lb) ; caisse maximale 101 × 68 × 81 cm.

Dois-je réserver longtemps à l'avance ?

Oui. Le nombre d'animaux est limité sur chaque vol et il est fortement recommandé de réserver leur transport dès l'achat du billet.

Les formalités du pays restent-elles obligatoires ?

Toujours. L'accord de WestJet ne remplace jamais les exigences vétérinaires et douanières du pays de destination.

title: Flying with a Dog on Wizz Air
description: Complete guide to travelling with your dog on Wizz Air, including assistance dogs, restrictions, alternative airlines and practical advice.
html:
Overview

Wizz Air is one of Europe's fastest-growing ultra-low-cost airlines. From its bases across Central and Eastern Europe—including Budapest, Bucharest, Warsaw, Vienna, Abu Dhabi, Rome and London Luton—it serves more than 190 destinations throughout Europe, the Middle East and parts of North Africa.

For dog owners, Wizz Air applies a policy similar to that of Ryanair and easyJet. Companion dogs are not accepted, either in the passenger cabin or in the aircraft hold.

The only exception concerns recognised assistance dogs, which may travel free of charge on eligible flights, subject to advance notification and the required documentation.

If you are travelling with a pet dog, you will almost certainly need to choose another airline. MyDogCanFly automatically identifies these situations and recommends airlines serving the same route that accept companion dogs.

Why MyDogCanFly gives Wizz Air 1.4/5

Strengths

  • Clear, well-documented pet policy
  • Recognised assistance dogs travel in the cabin
  • Clear, documented booking process

Limitations

  • Companion dogs not carried (assistance dogs only)
  • Reservation required and limited pet capacity
  • Destination-country import paperwork required

Is Wizz Air a good choice?

For owners of companion dogs, no. Wizz Air does not transport pets as part of its commercial model. If your dog is not a recognised assistance dog, MyDogCanFly will generally recommend another airline operating the same route.

Companion dogs

Cabin transport: not accepted in the cabin

Companion dogs are not accepted in the passenger cabin.

Hold transport: not accepted in the hold

Wizz Air does not transport companion dogs in the aircraft hold.

Assistance dogs: recognised assistance dogs may travel free of charge on eligible Wizz Air routes. Passengers must notify the airline before departure and provide all required documentation. Depending on the destination, additional health documentation may also be required.

Travel Difficulty

🚫 Not available

This airline does not carry companion dogs (assistance dogs excepted). You will need to choose another airline.

Before booking

Before purchasing your ticket:

  • verify whether your dog qualifies as a recognised assistance dog;
  • check destination-country import requirements;
  • if travelling with a companion dog, choose another airline.

Booking first and checking the pet policy afterwards usually results in having to change your itinerary.

Common mistakes

Assuming all airlines transport pets

Many European low-cost airlines—including Wizz Air—do not.

Confusing assistance dogs with emotional support animals

Only recognised assistance dogs are accepted.

Booking before checking the airline's policy

Companion dogs cannot be added to an existing booking.

Forgetting destination-country regulations

Even recognised assistance dogs must comply with veterinary import requirements.

Expert advice

Wizz Air is not suitable for travelling with a companion dog. If you need to fly with your pet, MyDogCanFly can immediately recommend alternative airlines operating the same route that accept dogs in the cabin or hold.

Can my dog travel in the cabin?

not accepted in the cabin

Can my dog travel in the hold?

not accepted in the hold

Are assistance dogs accepted?

Yes, on eligible routes and subject to advance notification and documentation.

Should I book Wizz Air if I'm travelling with my pet dog?

In almost every case, no.

Aperçu

Wizz Air est l'une des principales compagnies aériennes ultra low-cost d'Europe. Depuis ses nombreuses bases, notamment Budapest, Bucarest, Varsovie, Vienne, Rome, Londres-Luton et Abou Dhabi, elle dessert près de 200 destinations en Europe, au Moyen-Orient et en Afrique du Nord.

Pour les propriétaires de chiens, la politique de Wizz Air est comparable à celle de Ryanair et d'easyJet. Les chiens de compagnie ne sont acceptés ni en cabine ni en soute.

La seule exception concerne les chiens d'assistance officiellement reconnus, qui peuvent voyager gratuitement sur certains itinéraires sous réserve d'une déclaration préalable et des justificatifs exigés.

Si tu voyages avec un chien de compagnie, il faudra pratiquement toujours choisir une autre compagnie aérienne. MyDogCanFly détecte automatiquement cette situation et tu propose immédiatement les compagnies desservant la même destination tout en acceptant les chiens.

Points forts

  • Politique animaux claire et bien documentée
  • Chiens d'assistance acceptés en cabine
  • Processus de réservation clair et documenté

Limites

  • Chiens de compagnie non transportés (chiens d'assistance uniquement)
  • Réservation obligatoire et capacité limitée
  • Formalités d'importation du pays de destination à prévoir

Wizz Air est-elle un bon choix ?

Pour un chien de compagnie, non. Le modèle économique de Wizz Air ne prévoit pas le transport des animaux domestiques. Si ton chien n'est pas un chien d'assistance reconnu, MyDogCanFly tu orientera généralement vers une autre compagnie aérienne desservant le même itinéraire.

Chien de compagnie ou chien d'assistance

Transport en cabine : non accepté en cabine

Les chiens de compagnie ne sont pas autorisés en cabine.

Transport en soute : non accepté en soute

Wizz Air n'accepte pas les chiens de compagnie en soute.

Chiens d'assistance : les chiens d'assistance officiellement reconnus peuvent voyager gratuitement sur les vols éligibles. Ils doivent être déclarés avant le départ et être accompagnés des documents demandés par la compagnie. Selon le pays de destination, des formalités sanitaires complémentaires peuvent également être exigées.

Difficulté du voyage

🚫 Non disponible

Cette compagnie ne transporte pas les chiens de compagnie (chiens d'assistance exceptés). Il faudra choisir une autre compagnie.

Avant de réserver

Avant d'acheter ton billet :

  • vérifie si ton chien bénéficie officiellement du statut de chien d'assistance ;
  • consulte les formalités sanitaires du pays de destination ;
  • si tu voyages avec un chien de compagnie, choisis directement une autre compagnie.

Réserver un billet Wizz Air avant de consulter sa politique concernant les animaux conduit très souvent à devoir modifier tout son voyage.

Erreurs fréquentes

Penser que toutes les compagnies low-cost acceptent les chiens

Comme Ryanair et easyJet, Wizz Air refuse les animaux de compagnie.

Confondre chien d'assistance et animal de soutien émotionnel

Seuls les chiens d'assistance officiellement reconnus sont acceptés.

Réserver avant de consulter la politique de la compagnie

Les chiens de compagnie ne peuvent pas être ajoutés après la réservation.

Oublier les formalités du pays de destination

Même les chiens d'assistance doivent respecter les exigences vétérinaires et douanières du pays d'arrivée.

Conseil d'expert

Wizz Air n'est pas une compagnie adaptée aux propriétaires de chiens de compagnie. Avant de réserver, utilise MyDogCanFly pour identifier immédiatement les compagnies desservant le même itinéraire et acceptant les chiens en cabine ou en soute. Tu éviterez ainsi d'acheter un billet incompatible avec ton voyage.

FAQ

Mon chien peut-il voyager en cabine ?

non accepté en cabine

Mon chien peut-il voyager en soute ?

non accepté en soute

Les chiens d'assistance sont-ils acceptés ?

Oui. Les chiens d'assistance officiellement reconnus sont acceptés sur les itinéraires éligibles, sous réserve d'une déclaration préalable et des justificatifs demandés.

Dois-je réserver Wizz Air si je voyage avec mon chien ?

Dans la quasi-totalité des cas, non. Il est préférable de choisir directement une compagnie aérienne acceptant les animaux de compagnie.
